about: MUTATING — upgrade the forge's Forgejo to a newer release (infra/forge/upgrade-forgejo.sh <version> <plan_sha256>): changes the ONE image line of /opt/forgejo/docker-compose.yml from codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:<from> to :<version> and recreates the one container with docker compose up -d --no-deps --pull never forgejo, on the system docker daemon. Built as backlog cecf62b3 (the 2026-10-18 command-line gap inventory: no runbook and no verb upgraded Longhorn, Kubernetes or Forgejo, so each was a hand session; David 2026-10-18: every infra act is a website-approved verb); Forgejo is the first of the three because its install is one container declared by one compose file the tree already reads. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape, as restart-forgejo and move-forgejo-data are: it declares requires_approval with plan-a-forgejo-upgrade (this script's --plan) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan — the version diff, the health preconditions and the rollback target — onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders, every check again, and changes nothing unless today's plan hashes to it (exit 78). After a run Forgejo runs the target, so the same approval re-renders as 'already runs' and is refused: at most once. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM: the image repository is fixed in the script; the version param is digits only and must be strictly newer than what runs and at most one major release ahead; the target is named on the signed plan by image id, and the write refuses if the local tag names another; the compose file must carry exactly one line declaring the running image, and the staged file must differ from it in exactly that line and read, by compose's own reading, as the target. EACH STEP RE-READS THE PRECONDITIONS: the container running the plan's image, /api/healthz passing and no CI job container (FORGEJO-ACTIONS-*) running are read at the render, immediately before the dump, after the dump, and immediately before the swap. Each boundary also refuses open trains or gates, running convergence, or a standing converge hold, and any that fails stops the run with Forgejo untouched (exit 78). THE ROLLBACK TARGET is taken before anything changes: a forgejo dump by forge-backup.sh (the nightly timer's one definition, verified before it is named; a dump that fails refuses the run), the compose file kept as <compose>.pre-upgrade-<from>, and the image <from> by id — all three printed on every outcome after the swap, with the fact that going back needs the dump's database as well as the old image. THE EFFECT IS READ BACK: every 5 s for up to 600 s (a release migrates its database on first start), the service's one container running the target's image id, /api/healthz passing, /api/v1/version saying the target, and refs/heads/main inside the container holding the main read before the swap; only when all four hold on two consecutive reads is the effect line printed, and otherwise the run exits 1 saying the upgrade is NOT proven, with what each read said and the rollback target. If compose up fails and the original container still runs the old image, the verb restores the original compose file. After recreation, recovery requires the named rollback artifacts. Timeout 1800: the re-render with its pull (up to 420 s), the dump (bounded by forge-backup's own 5 GiB ceiling), the swap, and the script's own 600 s read-back, which gives its verdict before the runner's kill.
effect: ^upgrade-forgejo: Forgejo upgraded [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ → [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ — read back: container [0-9a-f]+ runs image [a-z0-9]+:[0-9a-f]{64}, /api/healthz pass, /api/v1/version [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+, refs/heads/main holds [0-9a-f]+( \(main is now [0-9a-f]+\))?, on two reads [0-9]+s apart \(after [0-9]+s\)\. Rollback target: .+, compose file .+, database dump .+$
